product.name: BMN 270
product.vector_or_capsid: AAV5 capsid; expression cassette inserted between AAV2 ITRs
product.transgene: cDNA for the B-domain-deleted SQ FVIII with a hybrid human liver-specific transcription promoter (HLP)

evidence.quote: BMN 270, an Adeno-Associated Virus Vector–Mediated Gene Transfer of Human Factor VIII, with Prophylactic Corticosteroids in Hemophilia A Patients
Active Investigational Product: AAV5-hFVIII-SQ
BMN 270 is an AAV5-based gene therapy vector that expresses the SQ form of hFVIII under the control of a hybrid human liver-specific promoter (Figure 1).

BMN 270 contains the cDNA for the B-domain-deleted SQ FVIII with a hybrid human liver- specific transcription promoter (HLP). The expression cassette is inserted between AAV2 ITRs, and this genome is packaged in the AAV5 capsid.
Each subject will receive a single intravenous infusion of BMN 270 at 6E13 vg/kg.

BMN 270 is a sterile, clear, colorless-to-pale yellow solution for IV infusion and is supplied in a 10 mL Crystal Zenith® (CZ) vial. Each vial contains 8.5 mL (extractable volume 8 mL) of AAV5-hFVIII-SQ at a concentration of 2E13 vector genomes per mL in a pH 7.4 phosphate buffer.

All subjects will be started on prophylactic corticosteroids starting on the day of infusion (Day 1). The first dose of prophylactic corticosteroids (40 mg of prednisone or prednisolone, or an equivalent dose of another corticosteroid) should be taken at least 3 hours prior to the start of the BMN 270 infusion and continued on a daily basis.
in conjunction with receipt of a 19-week prophylactic corticosteroid regimen starting on the day of BMN 270 infusion
Dosages are for prednisone or an equivalent dose of another corticosteroid.

cross_references.soa_note: Refer to Table 9.7.8.2.1for laboratory assessments to be included and for complement panel tests, and to Table 9.7.8.4.1 for liver tests (LTs). LT assessment is weekly, but may be checked more frequently when ALT values are > ULN or ≥ 1.5x baseline value or based upon discussion between the Medical Monitor and the Investigator. Subjects with ALT > ULN or ≥ 1.5x baseline value during the study and either an alternative etiology considered or for further evaluation of the lab abnormality may undergo additional evaluations (eg, imaging studies including MRI or ultrasound, additional blood tests, and/or liver biopsy) at the discretion of the Investigator. Additional testing of FVIII and LTs during any study week may be performed if: the ALT has increased to ≥ 1.5x baseline value or >ULN or after a discussion between the Medical Monitor and the Investigator based on a review of subject data. If ALT values are stable over the course of several weeks, assessment of FVIII activity and ALT levels may be adjusted based on discussion between the Medical Monitor and the Investigator. In case of a safety concern, additional unscheduled laboratory tests may be performed locally (at the Investigator’s discretion) in order to facilitate timely and appropriate clinical management decisions; where possible, a matched sample for testing at the central laboratory should be collected (using the Unscheduled Visit lab kit) at the same time as the local unscheduled sample. While exploratory samples for cytokine profiling will be collected at the time points indicated above, testing of these samples will be performed only as deemed necessary by the Sponsor.

cross_references.soa_note: Following initiation or completion of corticosteroid regimen, if a recurrence of ALT values > ULN or ≥ 1.5x baseline value is reported, corticosteroid management decisions will be based on discussions between the Investigator and Medical Monitor. Modification of the corticosteroid regimen may take into consideration timing of ALT elevation (prior to or after Week 52), as well as possible confounders for the ALT elevation and adverse events related to corticosteroid dosing. Guidance for tapering oral corticosteroid dosing can be found in Section 9.4.8.2, although a discussion between the PI and Medical Monitor should take place prior to tapering the corticosteroid dose.
cross_references.target_heading: 9.4.8.2 Corticosteroid Treatment and/or Alternative Immunosuppressive Agent Treatment of Elevated Hepatic Transaminases
cross_references.what_it_says: Unless otherwise indicated, reactive corticosteroid treatment should be initiated at a dose of 60 mg/day. If the ALT level remains stable or declines after 2 weeks, consider gradual taper of corticosteroids: 40 mg/day for 3 weeks, 30 mg/day for 1 week, 20 mg/day for 1 week and 10 mg/day for 1 week.

evidence.quote: Corticosteroid Treatment and/or Alternative Immunosuppressive Agent Treatment of Elevated Hepatic Transaminases

Unless otherwise indicated, reactive corticosteroid treatment should be initiated at a dose of 60 mg/day. If the ALT level remains stable or declines after 2 weeks, consider gradual taper of corticosteroids: 40 mg/day for 3 weeks, 30 mg/day for 1 week, 20 mg/day for 1 week and 10 mg/day for 1 week.

notes: Document: Protocol 270-303, Amendment 2 (25 May 2021); Original Protocol 28 February 2020, Amendment 1 15 September 2020. Pages 403-423 are Section 25 (Protocol Amendment Text Revisions, redline of Amendment 1 with merged inserted/deleted text) and were not used as evidence. Product: no lymphodepleting product (not applicable to AAV gene therapy). Prophylactic corticosteroids (prednisone or prednisolone) recorded as a protocol-specified co-treatment; reactive corticosteroids and alternative immunosuppressants (tacrolimus or mycophenolate) are described in Section 9.4.8.2 but not recorded as products. BMN 270 manufacturing/source not stated; formulation (10 mL Crystal Zenith vial, 2E13 vg/mL, pH 7.4 phosphate buffer) is quoted in evidence only. Immunogenicity: specimen 'plasma and PBMCs' is the general statement of Section 9.7.4 for all immunogenicity assays; no per-assay specimen is printed except PBMCs for ELISpot. No specimen, method or lab stated for the CDx AAV5 TAb assay; titer cut-off stated as below the minimum required dilution (< 20); no units printed for TAb/TI. No lab stated for immunogenicity assays (Section 6 only says bioanalytical samples go to 'appropriate specialty laboratories'). Panels: Table 9.7.8.2.1 is laid out in columns whose text-layer order interleaves rows; analytes were assigned to columns by row order (Blood Chemistry / Hematology / Urine Tests / Coagulation Screen / Complement Panel / Other Tests). The placement of 'Bilirubin' and the second 'Glucose' in Urine Tests and of 'Glucose' in Blood Chemistry follows that reading; verify against the PDF page image (PDF p. 349). Specimen for panels not stated (synopsis safety list says 'serum chemistry and hematology' while Table 9.7.8.2.1 says 'Blood Chemistry'). Lab = central from the Section 6 statement 'Clinical Laboratory assessments will be performed at a nominated central laboratory'; unscheduled safety tests may be local with a matched central sample. Conflicts/variants: HLP is defined as 'hybrid human liver-specific promoter' in the abbreviation list (p.293) but 'human liver promoter' in the Figure 1 / Figure 7.3.1 legend (p.274, p.301). The liver-test panel in Table 9.7.8.4.1 includes Direct Bilirubin, the synopsis LT list does not. T1:j SoA note includes 'immunological' aspects for exploratory blood samples, the T2-3:e note and Section 9.7.7 do not. Section 9.4.8.2.2 contains a broken cross-reference ('refer to Error! Reference source not found.', p.338). Cross-references: all 12 targets found (Table 9.7.8.2.1 p.349, Table 9.7.8.4.1 p.351, Section 9.4.8.2 p.337 with taper guidance on p.338). Not found: biodistribution assays; vector integration or replication-competent virus testing; units for FVIII protein assay; specimen/method for HLA and FVIII genotyping. Abbreviations: the list on pp.292-294 is transcribed in full; additional entries come from the lab-table legends (pp.349, 351), Table 9.4.8.2.2.2 (p.340), the Figure 1 legend (p.274), and a few inline body definitions (HCC, ART, TGA, CZ, PRN, EQ VAS, ELF, MMRM). Tokens in SoA activity names not defined anywhere in the protocol: AAV5 (only AAV is defined), CDx, CK18, Grp78, DNA, ELISpot, EQ-5D-5L, FibroScan, FibroTest, Haemo-QoL-A, HCV, HDL, LDL, HIV, SARS-CoV-2 (and RT-PCR, Q4W/Q6W/Q12W, ABO, MRD in SoA notes/body). RBC is defined only in the Table 9.7.8.2.1 legend.
